All records provisional.

characters.summary: Gandalf the White possesses vastly increased power, authority, and resilience compared to his previous form, wielding the white staff and inspiring allies while intimidating foes. He fights with a combination of high-tier angelic presence, potent spellcasting, and expert swordsmanship with Glamdring.

techniques: Aura of blinding light and authority

mechanisms: Immunity to ordinary weapons through angelic nature

weaknesses: Physical embodiment limits the direct output of angelic power
Bound by the rules and limitations imposed by the Valar regarding direct domination
mobility: Rides Shadowfax, the chief of the Mearas
Standard foot movement with greatly enhanced vigor
limitations: Forbidden from matching Sauron in raw force or dominating free wills directly
characters.formDifferences: Upgraded from Gandalf the Grey with heightened spiritual power, authority, endurance, and dressed entirely in white.

sources.supports: General overview of Gandalf the White, his return, and his enhanced abilities in Tolkien's works.

feats.claim: Cast down Saruman's staff and broke his authority over Isengard.
feats.citation: The Two Towers, The White Rider

notableResults.citation: The Two Towers, The White Rider
notableResults.note: Stripped Saruman of his staff and expelled him from the Order of Wizards.

conditional.ability: Enhanced angelic power and white raiment
conditional.dependsOn: Sent back by Eru Ilúvatar with upgraded status

campaignTags.claim: Possesses inherent angelic magic and spellcasting capabilities as one of the Maiar.
Casts potent spoken spells and commands opponents using his staff and voice.

unknowns: Exact limits of his power when fully unconstrained outside of his physical guise.

characters.summary: Olórin in his uncloaked, divine form as a Maia in Valinor operates as a pure spiritual being of immense wisdom, pity, and light. Without the physical and mental limitations imposed by an aged human guise, his capabilities reflect his full angelic nature.

mechanisms: Incorporeal spiritual form immune to conventional physical harm

weaknesses: Cannot directly use overt military force or physical violence to conquer evil in Arda according to the decrees of the Valar
mobility: Spiritual flight and omnipresent wandering in Valinor
limitations: Subject to the counsel and hierarchy of the Valar
characters.formDifferences: Represents the character's primordial divine state before taking on the physical limitations of an old man as a Wizard in Middle-earth.

sources.supports: Background on Olórin as a Maia of Valinor before his incarnation as a wizard.

feats.claim: Resided in Valinor and walked among the Vanyar and Noldor, inspiring wisdom and love.

conditional.dependsOn: Operating outside of a physical incarnate body

campaignTags.claim: Is a Maia, an angelic immortal being possessing innate divine power.

unknowns: The full scope of combat capabilities before descending into physical form.

characters.continuity: The Lord of the Rings and The Silmarillion
characters.summary: Gil-galad was the last High King of the Noldor in Middle-earth, a legendary warrior-king who wielded the mighty spear Aeglos. He fought at the forefront of the Last Alliance of Elves and Men against Sauron.
weaknesses: Vulnerable to extreme heat and physical trauma as an incarnate Elf
mobility: Standard elven foot movement and mounted riding
limitations: Bounded by mortal physical limits of Middle-earth Elves

sources.supports: Details on Gil-galad, his role as High King, and his spear Aeglos.

feats.claim: Fought alongside Elendil to defeat Sauron at the slopes of Mount Doom, though at the cost of his own life.
feats.citation: The Fellowship of the Ring / The Silmarillion

notableResults.note: Slain in single combat alongside Elendil, though Sauron was also overthrown.

unknowns: The exact magical properties of his spear Aeglos beyond legend.

characters.summary: Gimli son of Glóin is a fierce and steadfast Dwarven warrior who relies on heavy armor, a broadaxe, and immense endurance. He excels in close-quarters melee combat, particularly in confined spaces like caves and fortifications.

mechanisms: Natural dwarven resistance to fatigue and physical punishment

weaknesses: Limited mobility and lack of ranged attacks aside from throwing weapons or a borrowed bow
Low speed compared to elves or mounted foes
mobility: Standard running and marching on foot
limitations: Cannot traverse long distances as quickly as Elves or mounted combatants

sources.supports: Overview of Gimli's weaponry, heritage, and role in the War of the Ring.

feats.claim: Slew forty-two Orcs during the Battle of Helm's Deep.
feats.citation: The Two Towers, The Helm's Deep

notableResults.note: Fought successfully in the Hornburg alongside Aragorn and Legolas.

unknowns: Performance against high-tier magical entities without magical assistance.

characters.summary: Glaurung, the Father of Dragons, is a massive, wingless reptile of immense physical strength who employs crushing jaws, devastating fire-breath, and powerful hypnotic psychological manipulation ("the glamour of Glaurung").

techniques: Physical crushing with massive bulk and tail sweeps

mechanisms: Impenetrable thick scales impervious to ordinary swords

weaknesses: The soft underbelly is vulnerable to powerful thrusts from legendary weapons wielded by exceptional heroes
mobility: Heavy crawling and walking speed across terrain
limitations: Wingless and therefore lacks flight mobility

sources.supports: Details on Glaurung's nature as the first dragon, fire-breath, and mind control abilities.

feats.claim: Racked and burned Eithel Sirion and drove back the Noldor forces during the Dagor Bragollach.
feats.citation: The Silmarillion, Of the Ruin of Beleriand

notableResults.citation: The Silmarillion, The Children of Húrin
notableResults.note: Successfully manipulated Túrin through psychological deception, though eventually slain by Túrin with Gurthang.

campaignTags.claim: Is a gargantuan dragon capable of crushing armies and structures.
Uses powerful hypnotic spells and gaze to control and deceive minds.

unknowns: Resistance to high-level angelic or divine magic.

characters.continuity: The Lord of the Rings and The Silmarillion
characters.summary: Glorfindel is a mighty Elf-lord of Rivendell restored to life with power akin to the Maiar. He moves with supernatural grace, fights with peerless swordsmanship, and possesses terrifying presence in the unseen spirit world.

techniques: Spiritual aura that strikes fear into Nazgûl

mechanisms: Dual existence in physical and spiritual realms

weaknesses: Bound by the physical laws of Middle-earth despite his elevated spiritual status
mobility: Rides Asfaloth without a saddle at high speed
Supernatural elven running speed and agility
limitations: Cannot be everywhere at once; deployed strategically by Elrond

sources.supports: Details on Glorfindel's resurrection, power, and encounter with the Nazgûl.

feats.claim: Slew a Balrog of Morgoth in single combat during the fall of Gondolin, dying in the process before being re-embodied.
feats.citation: The Silmarillion, Of the Fall of Gondolin

notableResults.citation: The Fellowship of the Ring, Flight to the Ford
notableResults.note: Single-handedly drove the Nazgûl into the Bruinen river through his terrifying presence.

campaignTags.claim: Possesses elevated spiritual power and presence comparable to the Eldar of Valinor.

unknowns: Exact upper limits of his combat output when fully unleashed.

characters.summary: Gollum is a wretched, corrupted creature who relies on stealth, surprise, biting, and strangulation. He avoids direct fair fights, preferring ambushes, shadows, and treacherous terrain.

mechanisms: Climbing ability on vertical rock faces to escape combat

weaknesses: Physically frail in direct combat against armed opponents
Weakened and burned by Elven rope and sunlight
limitations: Hates and is physically debilitated by direct sunlight and elven items

sources.supports: Overview of Gollum's physical traits, combat style, and reliance on stealth.

feats.claim: Strangled Déagol to take the One Ring.
feats.citation: The Fellowship of the Ring, The Shadow of the Past

notableResults.note: Amushed and strangled his companion over the Ring.

conditional.dependsOn: Possession and wearing of the One Ring

campaignTags.claim: Moves silently in the dark and stalks prey undetected for days.
Expert swimmer capable of catching fish in deep dark lakes.

characters.summary: Before taking the One Ring, Sméagol was a curious, river-dwelling hobbit-kindred creature who spent his time swimming, burrowing, and tracking secrets in dark places. He was not a combatant, relying on stealth and evasion.
weaknesses: Lack of combat training or martial weapons
limitations: No combat prowess or offensive magic
characters.formDifferences: Represents Sméagol prior to his complete physical and mental corruption by the One Ring.

sources.supports: Description of Sméagol's life among the River-folk before finding the Ring.

feats.claim: Explored deep tunnels and roots under the mountains before corruption set in.
feats.citation: The Fellowship of the Ring, The Shadow of the Past

campaignTags.claim: Lived by the river and was skilled at swimming and diving.
Prone to prying into secrets and moving unseen among his kin.

unknowns: Any documented physical combat wins prior to killing Déagol.

characters.summary: Gorbag is an Orc captain from Minas Morgul who fights with brutal, practical ruthlessness, utilizing a jagged blade, vicious cruelty, and tactical cunning typical of Mordor uruk-captains.
weaknesses: Prone to infighting and distrust with rival orc factions
mobility: Standard orc running and marching speed
limitations: Limited discipline outside of immediate fear of Sauron or the Nazgûl

sources.supports: General background on Orc captains like Gorbag and Shagrat during the War of the Ring.

feats.claim: Led a band of Mordor uruks in skirmishes and captured Frodo Baggins at Cirith Ungol.
feats.citation: The Return of the King, The Choices of Master Samwise

notableResults.citation: The Return of the King, The Choices of Master Samwise
notableResults.note: Slain by Shagrat during a bloody dispute over the mithril coat in the tower of Cirith Ungol.

unknowns: Exact combat feats outside of the skirmish at Cirith Ungol.
